newsitem.title: UK: Johnson Matthey profits rise, growth seen.
newsitem.headline: Johnson Matthey profits rise, growth seen.

text.p: British metals and materials group Johnson Matthey Plc on Thursday posted higher annual profits in line with analysts' estimates and predicted further growth this year.
The company's pretax profits rose 6.0 percent to 108.3 million pounds ($176.9 million) for the year to March 31, compared to analysts' forecasts of 105-110 million pounds.
Johnson Matthey also said it agreed with Japan's Kyocera Corp to license technology to each other for the packaging of microprocessors and semiconductors.
The firm's shares rose 23 pence to 484.5 by 0755 GMT.

"For the group as a whole, the coming year will be one of consolidation in some of our businesses but with growth coming from the Electronics Materials division and the Catalytic Systems division," the company said in its earnings statement.
It added that capital spending would be considerably below the average of two times depreciation it had invested over the last four years.

"The strategic development of Johnson Matthey as a leading global company in advanced materials technology remains on track, and we expect further milestones to be achieved during the coming year," the company said.
